0.heading: M K Sons Fine Jewels shares to list tomorrow; check latest GMP, expected listing price
0.intro: Shares of M K Sons Fine Jewels are set to make their stock market debut on Wednesday, November 4, with the latest grey market premium (GMP) indicating a potential listing gain of around 6 percent for investors.
0.body:
Shares of M K Sons Fine Jewels are set to make their stock market debut on Wednesday, November 4, with the latest grey market premium (GMP) indicating a potential listing gain of around 6 percent for investors.

The shares were commanding a grey market premium of Rs 10 apiece on November 3, as per InvestorGain. At the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 162, this translates into an estimated listing price of Rs 172 per share.

However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee the actual listing price. It can fluctuate ahead of the stock market debut.

Read Also: Former U-19 cricketer, failed IAS aspirant built Rs 100-crore café brand: Story of 'Yummy Bee' founder Sandeep Jangala

The Rs 275.4-crore initial public offering (IPO) of M K Sons Fine Jewels received an overall subscription of 5.09 times during its three-day bidding period, which closed on October 30.

The issue received bids for 6,05,95,171 shares against 1.19 crore shares on offer, according to NSE data.

Non-institutional investors (NIIs) led the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion 14.12 times. The retail investor category was subscribed 3.08 times, while the qualified institutional buyer (QIB) portion received 1.84 times bids.

The IPO opened for subscription on October 28, with the company fixing the price band at Rs 153-162 per share. At the upper end of the price band, the company was valued at around Rs 912 crore.

The Rs 275.4-crore public issue comprised a fresh issue of 1.36 crore equity shares worth Rs 220.32 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of shares worth Rs 55.08 crore.

While the proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company, the OFS proceeds will be received by the selling shareholder.

The minimum lot size for the IPO was 91 shares, requiring a minimum investment of Rs 14,742 at the upper end of the price band.

The company plans to utilise Rs 152.8 crore from the net proceeds to set up a new showroom in Maharashtra and expand an existing showroom in Gujarat. Another Rs 30 crore has been earmarked for debt repayment, while the remaining amount will be used for general corporate purposes.

Check IPO News Here

The basis of allotment was scheduled to be finalised on November 2. Refunds for unsuccessful applicants and the credit of allotted shares to demat accounts are scheduled for November 3.

The company's shares will list on both the BSE and NSE on November 4.

Aryaman Financial Services is the book-running lead manager to the issue, while Bigshare Services is the registrar.

About M K Sons Fine Jewels

Mumbai-based M K Sons Fine Jewels is engaged in the retailing of gold, diamond and cubic zirconia (CZ) jewellery through its showrooms.

The company currently operates five showrooms, including three in Mumbai and two in Ahmedabad. Its proposed expansion in Maharashtra and Gujarat is aimed at increasing its retail presence.

The company offers jewellery across different categories and designs, catering to customers through its physical retail network.

1.headline: Chartered Speed to supply e-buses to Bengaluru's BMTC from April; plans overhead charging system
1.heading: Chartered Speed to supply e-buses to Bengaluru's BMTC from April; plans overhead charging system
1.intro: Ahmedabad-based operator is exploring overhead charging infrastructure at BMTC depots to address space constraints. The 12-metre buses will have a range of up to 250 km on a single charge.
1.body:
Chartered Speed Limited plans to begin supplying electric buses to Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) in April-May 2027.

Ahmedabad-based firm is exploring overhead charging infrastructure at BMTC depots to address space constraints. Under the proposed system, buses would be parked beneath charging gantries, freeing up space compared with conventional ground-mounted chargers.

“We are looking at models being used in China and Europe, where charging infrastructure is installed overhead rather than on the ground. This will help unlock considerable space, particularly in a city like Bengaluru, where land availability is a major constraint,” Sanyam Gandhi, whole-time director of Chartered Speed, told Moneycontrol.

Also, read: MC Impact: Karnataka approves 4,500 PM E-DRIVE e-buses for Bengaluru; BMTC fleet to cross 10,000

“Charging a bus would take around one to one-and-a-half hours. An overhead pantograph will connect to a compatible charging point, typically located on the bus roof. Multiple buses could charge simultaneously, subject to the number of charging points and the depot's power capacity,” he said.

BMTC is planning to induct 4,500 e-buses under the PM E-DRIVE scheme. In the AC bus category, GreenCell Mobility emerged as the lowest bidder, quoting Rs 70.65 per km for 300 12-metre buses and Rs 60.94 per km for 100 9-metre buses. In the non-AC category, Chartered Speed quoted Rs 62.92 per km for 3,500 12-metre buses, while PMI Electro Mobility quoted Rs 55.55 per km for 600 9-metre buses.

“Chartered Speed bid for 3,500 buses, of which we are expected to receive orders for 50 percent, or 1,750 buses,” Gandhi said.

Under a 12-year contract, Chartered Speed will supply 12-metre, low-floor, non-AC buses in partnership with EKA Mobility. The buses will be manufactured in Pune and Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh, using a platform brought to India from European manufacturer VDL Bus and Coach.

Buses to have a range of up to 250 km

The company has simulated the buses' performance under BMTC's peak-hour operating conditions.

“The simulations assumed that buses would operate at more than 100 percent passenger load for 25 percent of the time (peak hours), at full capacity for 40 percent, and at around 60 percent capacity during the remaining 35 percent,” Gandhi said.

The buses achieved a simulated range of around 250 km on a single charge, with around 15 percent battery reserve. Actual daily distances are expected to vary between 170 km and 250 km. Opportunity charging will be important for routes exceeding 200 km, he added.

Safety and driver training

The buses will be equipped with CCTV cameras, wheelchair access and designated spaces for persons with disabilities. The company will also monitor vehicle health and driver behaviour.

Gandhi said Chartered Speed would handle driver recruitment and training in-house. Drivers will undergo mandatory training, quarterly refresher programmes and simulator sessions.

Depot readiness crucial for rollout

BMTC expects the depots to be made available from March-April 2027. Converting an existing depot to accommodate electric buses would take 45-60 days, including the installation of transformers, chargers and cables.

“If things progress as per the expected timeline, bus deliveries can begin from April or May 2027,” Gandhi said.

IPO and BMTC procurement

Chartered Speed is preparing for an initial public offering (IPO). Gandhi said the company was in the process of filing its Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus (UDRHP), followed by the Red Herring Prospectus (RHP), subject to regulatory approvals. The IPO is expected to take place in the current calendar year. The company is also pursuing corporate transport contracts in Bengaluru.

2.headline: Bombay Coated & Special Steels IPO allotment today; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar
2.heading: Bombay Coated & Special Steels IPO allotment today; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar
2.intro: The allotment of Bombay Coated & Special Steels' initial public offering (IPO) is expected to be finalised on November 3, following a strong response from investors. The Rs 183.06-crore IPO was subscribed 60.77 times by the close of bidding on November 2, according to exchange data.
2.body:
The allotment of Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels' initial public offering (IPO) is expected to be finalised on November 3, following a strong response from investors. The Rs 183.06-crore IPO was subscribed 60.77 times by the close of bidding on November 2, according to exchange data.

The issue received bids for more than 13.5 crore shares against approximately 2.23 crore shares on offer. Non-institutional investors (NIIs) led the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion 158.32 times. The qualified institutional buyer (QIB) category was subscribed 35.50 times, while the retail investor portion received 33.73 times subscription.

In the grey market, Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels shares were commanding a premium of around 11 percent on November 2, according to InvestorGain.

Read Also: BLS Polymers shares make blockbuster debut at 65% premium on NSE — should you buy, sell or hold?

However, the grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee listing gains. It can fluctuate before the stock market debut and should not be treated as a prediction of the actual listing price.

The company's shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on November 5.

Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels IPO allotment status: How to check

Investors can check their allotment status online once the basis of allotment is finalised.

Check allotment status on KFin Technologies

Step 1. Visit the KFin Technologies IPO allotment website at https://ipostatus.kfintech.com/
Step 2. Select Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels from the list of issues, once available.
Step 3. Choose an identification option, such as PAN or application number.
Step 4. Enter the required details and submit.
Step 5. Your allotment status will be displayed on the screen.

Check allotment status on BSE

1. Visit the BSE IPO application status page at https://www.bseindia.com/investors/appli_check
2. Select 'Equity' as the issue type.
3. Choose Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels from the IPO list.
4. Enter your application number or PAN, as requested.
5. Submit the details to view your allotment status.

Check IPO bid details on NSE

Step 1. Visit the NSE IPO bid verification page at https://www.nseindia.com/invest/check-trades-bids-verify-ipo-bids
Step 2. Select the relevant IPO from the issue list.
Step 3. Enter the required application details and submit to verify your bid.
Step 4. Your allotment status will be displayed on the screen.

The IPO opened for subscription on October 29 and closed on November 2. The company fixed the price band at Rs 78 to Rs 82 per share.

The minimum lot size was 182 shares, translating into an investment of Rs 14,924 at the upper end of the price band.

The Rs 183.06-crore IPO comprises an entirely fresh issue of approximately 2.23 crore equity shares. The company will receive the proceeds from the offering to fund its business requirements.

Check IPO News Here

Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels plans to use Rs 125 crore from the net proceeds to repay or prepay certain borrowings. Another Rs 15.77 crore has been earmarked for costs associated with acquiring capital equipment under existing lease arrangements with Siemens Financial Services Private Limited. The remaining amount will be used for general corporate purposes.

The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on November 3. Refunds for unsuccessful applicants and credit of allotted shares to demat accounts are scheduled for November 4, ahead of the November 5 listing.

Smart Horizon Capital Advisors is the book-running lead manager to the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.

About Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels

Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels is a steel processing company that converts steel coils into processed steel products through operations such as slitting, cut-to-length processing, shearing and embossing.

Its products cater to industrial customers that require processed steel for their manufacturing operations. The company's manufacturing facilities are located in Wada and Bhiwandi in Maharashtra, Ghiloth in Rajasthan, and Sri City in Andhra Pradesh.
